title: Stars and Galaxies
summary: What stars are, how they are born, why they twinkle and how big the Universe is.

steps.title: A star is a Sun
sentences: Every star you see at night is a sun, a huge ball of hot gas making its own light.
They look tiny only because they are extremely far away.
After the Sun, the nearest star to us is Proxima Centauri, about 4.2 light-years away.

steps.title: What is a light-year?
sentences: A light-year is a distance, not a time.
It is how far light travels in one year, about nine and a half trillion kilometres.
So when you see a star 100 light-years away, you are seeing light that left it 100 years ago.
points: Looking far means looking back in time

steps.title: Birth and death of a star
sentences: Stars are born inside clouds of gas and dust that clump together under gravity.
They shine for millions or billions of years by joining tiny atoms together in their cores.
When a star runs out of fuel it changes, and very large stars end in a huge explosion called a supernova.
points: Born in gas and dust clouds

steps.title: Galaxies
sentences: A galaxy is a giant family of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity.
Our home is the Milky Way, which has more than a hundred billion stars.
There are billions of other galaxies in the Universe.
points: We live in the Milky Way

facts: Stars twinkle because their light wobbles as it passes through moving layers of Earth's air. Planets usually twinkle less.
The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old.
The Milky Way is so wide that light takes roughly 100,000 years to cross it.

quiz.why: It is the distance light travels in one year.

quiz.q: Why do stars look so tiny?
quiz.why: Stars are huge, but they are trillions of kilometres away.

quiz.q: What is the name of our galaxy?
quiz.why: We live in the Milky Way galaxy.
